Perform an automated Spec Quality & Completeness Audit on the generated specification:

1. Inspect `specs/<feature>/spec.md` (or the active feature spec).
2. Verify the specification against deterministic SDD quality criteria:
   - User Stories & Value: Every story defines clear actor, action, and expected business outcome.
   - Acceptance Criteria: Every story includes unambiguous Given/When/Then scenarios.
   - Robustness & Edge Cases: Explicitly defines error handling, network/storage failures, empty states, and validation boundaries.
   - Architectural Boundaries: Enforces Clean Architecture / vertical slice boundaries without leaking infrastructure details.
3. Generate `specs/<feature>/SPEC_AUDIT.md` with:
   - Executive Quality Score (0-100%) and Pass/Fail status (threshold: 90%)
   - Scenario Matrix: list of covered user journeys and edge cases
   - Remediation: if any criteria are ambiguous or missing, update `spec.md` directly to satisfy them.
4. Output a concise 5-line executive summary in the terminal.

output.prompt:
Generate high-fidelity UI screens and canonical design tokens using Google Stitch MCP:

EXECUTION PROTOCOL:
- Execute all Stitch MCP tools directly in this conversation. Do NOT delegate Stitch tool calls or verification to subagents (subagents lack access to MCP extensions).
- TEXT-ONLY ASSETS RULE: Never attempt to download binary screenshots, create fake .png files, or call `read_file` on any `.png` file. In Gemini CLI, reading ASCII text with a `.png` extension triggers fatal Google API 400 codec errors. The complete visual design master is the HTML code (`<screen-id>.html`).

STEPS:
0. Idempotency Check: Inspect `specs/<feature>/designs/`. If `.html` screens, `tokens.css`, and `routes-manifest.json` already exist, verify their completeness, ensure fixtures exist, and output the summary table immediately without re-generating from scratch.
1. Inspect `specs/<feature>/spec.md` and `plan.md` to identify the core user journeys and all required screens/views.
2. Locate or create the feature designs directory at `specs/<feature>/designs/` and subdirectory `specs/<feature>/designs/fixtures/`.
3. Invoke Google Stitch MCP tools directly:
   - Call `create_project` (or target active project) with the feature title.
   - Call `create_design_system` to establish color palette, typography (Inter/Roboto), corner roundness, and appearance theme aligned with the project.
   - For each primary screen described in the specification, call `generate_screen_from_text` with rich layout, accessibility, and component details.
   - Call `get_screen` for each generated screen to retrieve its `html_code` reference.
   - Download ONLY the HTML code using `download_file` with `name: <screen.html_code.name>`:
     * Save the HTML code to `specs/<feature>/designs/<screen-id>.html` using `write_file`.
     * Do NOT call `download_file` on `screenshot.name`. The HTML file contains the full markup, CSS tokens, and layout.
4. Extract and create the canonical design tokens stylesheet at `specs/<feature>/designs/tokens.css`:
   - Define CSS variables under `:root` for colors (`--color-background`, `--color-surface`, `--color-primary`, `--color-text`, etc.), radii (`--radius-sm`, `--radius-md`, `--radius-lg`), typography (`--font-family`, `--font-size-*`), and spacing (`--space-*`).
5. Create `specs/<feature>/designs/routes-manifest.json` following `.specify/templates/routes-manifest.json.tmpl`:
   - Map each screen to its local development route (e.g. `/`, `/analytics`), title, DOM test selector, and fixture mock data path.
   - Generate declared fixture JSON mock files in `specs/<feature>/designs/fixtures/`.
6. Fallback Resilience: If Google Stitch MCP is unavailable or encounters connection/rate-limit errors, generate clean wireframe HTML files directly (`<screen-id>.html`), `tokens.css`, and `routes-manifest.json`. Do NOT create dummy `.png` files.
7. Output a summary table in the terminal listing all generated screens, HTML files, and token variables.

This feature includes UI components.
Before the human design review gate, perform an Impeccable Design Critique:

1. Activate the `impeccable` skill using the `activate_skill(name: 'impeccable')` tool (do NOT use `read_file` on external paths outside the workspace) and review the UI architecture:
   - If Stitch was enabled: inspect screens in `specs/<feature>/designs/*.html` and `tokens.css`.
   - If Stitch was NOT enabled: inspect UI wireframes, component contracts, and design tokens specified in `plan.md`.
2. Evaluate visual hierarchy, cognitive load (Operate vs Persuade), contrast ratios (WCAG AA), typographic rhythm, and Tailwind/shadcn tokens.
3. Generate `specs/<feature>/designs/DESIGN_CRITIQUE.md` with:
   - Executive Assessment
   - Heuristic Findings
   - Actionable Adjustments (or Stitch edit_screens prompts)
4. Output a concise 5-line summary for the human reviewer in the terminal.

output.prompt:
Perform empirical verification of the completed implementation:

1. Inspect `specs/<feature>/spec.md`, `tasks.md`, test outputs, and quality gate results.
2. If this feature has UI (`has_ui: true`):
   - Activate the `impeccable` skill using the `activate_skill(name: 'impeccable')` tool (do NOT use `read_file` on external paths outside the workspace) and perform a comprehensive Accessibility & Design Audit (`impeccable audit` checklist: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, keyboard navigation `:focus-visible`, minimum 44px touch targets, and responsive layout scaling).
   - Confirm micro-interactions and transitions respect `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (`impeccable animate`).
3. Verify each acceptance scenario (Given/When/Then) against concrete empirical evidence:
   - Unit, integration, and regression tests passing with zero failures
   - Clean Architecture boundary validation passing (`vp check`)
   - Route & component contracts and ghost classes passing (`check-contracts.sh`)
   - Visual fidelity & Stitch token tests passing (`verify-stitch-design.sh`)
   - Production bundle budget passing (`check-bundle-budget.sh`)
4. Generate `specs/<feature>/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md` with:
   - Scenario Verification Matrix (Pass/Fail per acceptance criterion)
   - Empirical Evidence Log (test names, gate outputs, screenshots, audit findings)
   - Delta-Spec Sync: Document any architectural clarifications or domain adjustments made during implementation.
5. Output an Executive Closing Summary in the terminal for asynchronous human review.
